change_vs_ref: + --aug_apm_p 0.6 (WebRTC NS pass on 60% of clips; --aug_apm_ns_levels left at default 6 12 18 21)
rationale:
This is iteration d, the conditional last slot of the B4 screen (max_iterations 4). The wave.json lever_notes say: "if opus_plc is 'positive' on the WF1 CI rule, run its pre-registered zero-loss control ... Otherwise pick the best-supported B4 follow-up from the analyst's proposals (B4 flags only)." B4b (opus_plc) is "null (inside +-0.5)" on both readouts (iter02/verdict.json: merge +0.24 [-0.30, +0.78], final +0.12 [-0.48, +0.71]), so the zero-loss control is not triggered. user_notes.md has one note: judge arms on the verdict.json verdicts (B4a: merge revisit, final promote/positive). It does not change the queue. Base = B2f, because rules.keep_best keeps it as the reference for the whole wave.

Why the apm_ns dose step (analyst rank 1 in the B4c analyze.result.json):
- B4a (`--aug_apm_p 0.3`) is the only B4 arm with a positive verdict. iter01/verdict.json gives final 93.15 vs 92.14, delta +1.02, CI [+0.43, +1.60] (positive, promote) and merge 92.55 vs 91.98, delta +0.57, CI [-0.01, +1.17] (above band, CI includes 0).
- The two later arms were both null, so they now act as equal-dose placebos for "generic extra 30% DSP augmentation": B4b +0.24 / +0.12 and B4c +0.03 / +0.20. The B4a gain is therefore not explained by adding any DSP stage at p 0.3.
- B4a's gain sits where the largest remaining error sits, the noisy bona false alarms (B4c report §5.4 / largest_remaining_error). Half-B noisy bona FA fell 213 -> 192 (merge) and 210 -> 177 (final); saturated FA 136 -> 114 / 133 -> 123; mean noisy EER 10.09 -> 9.53 / 9.66 -> 9.16. It also has the wave's smallest oracle gap (0.43 / 0.10).
- The exp-design skill allows a one-flag dose step after a clear positive. The open question for the owner at wrapup is whether B4a's gain is real and dose-responsive, or a single-seed fluctuation whose merge CI touches 0. Doubling p is the one flag-level test of that.

Why not the others:
- Rank 2, `--aug_apm_ns_levels 18 21` at p 0.3: it chases the secondary afftdn-vs-anlmdn contrast (B4a -1.39 / -1.14, rank 1 of 3). B4a's primary NS contrast is REFUTED on the final (DiD +0.49), and placebo B4c beats it (-0.07, B4c report §2.6). It also leaves open whether the outcome gain itself repeats.
- Rank 3, the opus zero-loss control: its pre-registered trigger (opus_plc positive) did not fire, and there is no B4b gain to attribute.
- Rank 4, `--aug_dtx_p 1.0`: by the B4c analyst's own account, dose_ratio stays near 0.03 ("under-dosed"). B4c also broke the matched R_spoof must-not-move item (-0.69 on both readouts).
- Rank 5, the seed repeat: --seed is outside `allowed` (wave seed pinned to 1234), the owner declined a B2f replicate, and configuration levers remain.

Constraints:
- `--aug_apm_p` is in `allowed`. It is coupled with `--aug_apm_ns_levels`, which stays at its default 6 12 18 21, so this is one factor.
- validate_b4_args only requires 0 <= p <= 1.
- Nothing forbidden or fixed is touched. num_epochs stays 8 (max 10), batch_size 16, seed 1234.

Risks recorded in the B4a report that a higher dose could amplify:
- half-B heldout spoof misses 16 -> 23 / 14 -> 19;
- heldout English bona recall 56.6 / 58.9;
- train loss above B2f's at every epoch (ep8 0.0562 vs 0.0501);
- ep1 TrainAcc 86.88 vs 87.36.
These are written into the falsifier.
hypothesis: B4a's half-B gain comes from the WebRTC NS pass and grows with exposure. Training both classes on suppressor-processed noisy audio pulls noisy bona out of the movable false-alarm band and puts the operating point at p = 0.5. Equal-dose arms on other DSP slots were null (B4b, B4c), so the effect is specific to the NS pass, not generic augmentation. At p = 0.6 the gain should hold or grow, and the merge CI low should clear 0.
falsifier:
(1) No dose response: a final delta vs B2f < +0.5, or a merge delta below B4a's +0.57 together with a final below B4a's +1.02 by more than the ±0.5 band. Either means B4a's gain was not dose-driven (or was seed noise); close the flag-level apm_ns line and do not promote B4a without a seed replicate.
(2) Trade-off: half-B heldout spoof misses above B4a's 23 / 19, matched or heldout R_spoof down > 0.5, or full-set offline-NS spoof misses > 29. More NS buys bona recall with spoof recall ('NS => bona'); drop the higher dose.
(3) Lost raw-noise exposure: WF1 delta < -0.5 with matched F1 down > 1.0 vs B2f; drop.
(4) Clean guard: dev_online_clean F1 down > 0.5; drop.
(5) Shared under-fit: ep1 TrainAcc < 85.36 or ep8 TrainLoss > 0.0752, together with heldout bona recall down; confounded.
(6) Mechanism (secondary): afftdn-vs-anlmdn DiD > -0.84 (the panel mean) on the final; the harsh-suppressor signal does not scale with dose.
Verdict rule (wave): positive = merge half_B WF1 delta > +0.5 with CI low > 0 and clean drop <= 0.5; |delta| <= 0.5 = null.
header_text:
B4d = B2f + --aug_apm_p 0.6. This is the apm_ns dose step and the conditional iteration d of the B4 screen (rdloop B4 module b4wave). Each training clip, of either class, has a 60% chance of one pass through the standalone WebRTC NoiseSuppressor (pywebrtc_audio, NS only, no HPF/AGC/AEC). The pass runs after the acoustic stage and before the codec, from the separate B4 RNG stream. The suppression level is drawn uniformly from the default 6/12/18/21 dB (--aug_apm_ns_levels unchanged).

Why: opus_plc (B4b) was null on both readouts, so the pre-registered zero-loss control is not triggered. The analyst's best-supported follow-up is the dose step of B4a, the only positive arm: final +1.02 [+0.43, +1.60], merge +0.57 [-0.01, +1.17] vs B2f. The equally dosed 30% arms B4b (+0.24 / +0.12) and B4c (+0.03 / +0.20) were null.

Target: the noisy bona false alarms, the largest remaining error. Half-B noisy FA were B2f 213 / 210 and B4a 192 / 177; mean noisy EER was B2f 10.09 / 9.66 and B4a 9.53 / 9.16. The run should lift the merge readout's CI low above 0.

Guards: clean F1 within 0.5, R_spoof within 0.5 on every set, heldout spoof misses <= B4a's 23 / 19, offline-NS spoof misses <= 29.

Everything else is B2f's argv: 8 epochs, batch 16, seed 1234.
